status: RE-RECORDED 2026-09-22 — supersedes the 2026-09-18 file (rings A/B/S measured on a spare iPhone kit that was no longer available on the day of the photo run). Truth values below come from the on-screen gauge, not from the app. Full disclosure: the raw photos were run through the evaluator in triage mode on 2026-09-21/22 while the pipeline gates were being calibrated (see DELIVERY-NOTES → What changed after the first photos); the gauge readings were taken before that and were not adjusted afterwards.
scaleCheck: screen-kit.html on a MacBook Air (13.3", 2560×1600 panel, 1440×900 CSS): an ID-1 bank card's long edge (85.60 mm) matched the calibration line at 5.03 CSS px/mm; the panel's nominal pitch gives 2560 / 286.5 mm / 1.778 = 5.03 as well. Independent check on the photos: the display's pixel grid (0.1119 mm pitch) resolved by FFT on H-paper-05 gives 24.6–24.9 photo px/mm against 24.67 from the marker.
kit: screen-kit.html on the MacBook Air laid flat (5.03 CSS px/mm); the ring lies on a square of white paper placed on the glass inside the zone for the *-paper-* photos and directly on the glass for the *-glass-* photos. Photos with an iPhone main camera, hand-held, roughly overhead, 11–21 cm from the sheet (distance estimated from the marker's size). No printer was available.

H.kind: hinged hoop, black, solid band ≈ 3.3 mm wide (outer ≈ 24.3 mm); the hinge and the clasp gap interrupt the inner rim
H.method: on-screen gauge (screen-kit.html → Gauge, 0.1 mm steps), ring centred on the circle, read by eye from ≈ 30 cm: L = 17.4 (largest circle fully visible inside the hole), U = 17.6 (smallest the ring covers) → 17.5. Cross-checked by photo: with the 17.5 mm circle under the ring the line is visible along two opposite sides of the hole; with 17.9 mm the line is covered everywhere (photos IMG_3610 / IMG_3609, kept out of the test set — no marker in frame).

B.kind: hammered open band, silver-coloured, ≈ 0.9 mm wide radially (outer ≈ 18.7 mm); the hole is visibly out of round (facets)
B.method: on-screen gauge, same procedure as H: L = 16.7, U = 16.9 → 16.8. Because the hole is faceted, 'fully visible' is a judgement of the narrowest direction — matches what the app reports (largest inscribed circle).

photoNotes.U-no-marker.jpg: ring on paper on a blank white screen — the marker is not in the frame
photoNotes.U-blur-heavy.jpg: motion-blurred so heavily that the marker itself is not detected; the intended verdict was BLUR, the honest expectation is NO_MARKER because the marker gate runs first
photoNotes.pending: U-tilt40, U-two-rings and a mild U-blur (marker still detectable) are requested and will be appended in a later commit if they arrive before submission
